directions.q073_bargain:
PRESERVE the user-approved composition and NPCs, but redraw in the latest FOUR-COLOR PARCHMENT rendering, exactly one base and one shadow per material. All old color names below mean their equivalent parchment/sepia value only. A rare-herb grower and a healer are considering shared cultivation so the marsh will not be stripped bare. ONLY TWO local adults: the older male herbalist, lean and slightly stooped, grey hair tied back and a short beard, in an olive cloak; and one practical adult female healer with a cream headscarf and rolled sleeves. They have not agreed yet.

Compose from a slightly raised oblique viewpoint across a narrow marsh growing bed. At the LEFT third the herbalist crouches on a worn plank edge, a protective forearm resting on his CLOSED brown leather backpack; his other hand indicates ONE sparse surviving herb clump. At the RIGHT midground the healer kneels beside a small empty seed tray, attentive and reserved rather than smiling or making a sales gesture. A thin strip of water separates their working positions. The vulnerable root clump and closed bag form one connected focal area. No desk, book, map, jars, second healer, visiting hero or village crowd.

Broad dark olive reed silhouettes along one edge; a quiet flat slate-blue water shape takes most of the top-right background. Cool overcast daylight with restrained warm highlights on the hands and herb leaves. Only two or three flat shapes per reed clump; no intricate vegetation. Keep the bodies and faces understated, and make the bargaining hesitation readable through their distance and posture. REPAIR PRIORITY: keep the two small local NPCs and the meaningful marsh gap, but replace ALL water and foliage flecks with large clean connected flat two-tone shapes. No isolated texture pixels, dither, speckled edges or leafy carpet. Quiet water and background should be perfectly uniform broad masses.
directions.q090_offer:
PRESERVE the user-approved composition and NPCs, but redraw in the latest FOUR-COLOR PARCHMENT rendering, exactly one base and one shadow per material. All old color names below mean their equivalent parchment/sepia value only. At first encounter, an undead commander ignores unarmed travellers and is quietly gathering the swords of his own fallen soldiers. Show ONLY ONE undead commander. No living visitor, hero, merchant, grieving family, audience or extra undead army; those would belong to other phases. No gore.

Very wide low horizon composition. Most of the LEFT and upper frame is a quiet empty flat grey-blue dawn sky and a low desolate battlefield silhouette. On the RIGHT lower third the gaunt commander kneels on one knee, worn simple armour and a ragged muted burgundy cape hanging heavily. He carefully lays one battered plain sword beside TWO other mismatched fallen comrades' blades, all three forming a small modest parallel row on a scrap of old cloth. The hilt under his hand catches the strongest small light in the scene. His bowed head is almost just a pale bone profile and shadow; restrained and mournful, not a detailed horror skull or theatrical villain pose. The hands, blade and scabbards must stay clearly separate and continuous.

A single broken standard leans behind him, with a short torn banner kept broad and plain. Foreground grass is two or three dark clusters and a broad mound, not a carpet of noise. Pale dawn against near-charcoal silhouette and subdued rust-red cloth, no glowing magic, ornate gravestones, speckled fog or dramatic cinematic lighting. The scene should communicate an unfinished act of remembrance through space and gesture alone. REPAIR PRIORITY: keep solitary commander and exactly three swords in the lower right, but sky, horizon and cloth must be perfectly FLAT color masses without any tiny isolated marks or surface speckles. Simplify contour transitions into deliberate connected native pixel clusters. Two tones per material, no extra modeling.
